answer: In a bonded vouching scheme, a new agent can't act until an established one stakes slashable collateral to bridge it into the trust graph. If the newcomer misbehaves, that bond is burned, so the voucher carries real risk. Spinning up sybils is like cracking a walnut with no meat inside: each fake needs its own deposit, so an attacker's cost scales linearly with the number of identities. Reputation can't be brushed on like cheap pigment; it accrues only through honest, bonded history that is expensive to fake at scale.
